The second experiment with added product slightly separated M17 (P+catS deactivation) as the best, but most mechanisms are still within ~0.5 NLL units of each other. M4, M5 are clearly eliminated. M3 is poor. The remaining 17 mechanisms are still hard to distinguish. Need more discriminating conditions.
</reflection>

<hypothesis>
The regimes I haven't explored are:
1. **High catalyst concentration** - will amplify catalyst dimerization (M2, M13) and catalyst-catalyst deactivation (M13, M19). At high [cat], M2/M13 would show lower-than-expected activity due to cat2 formation.
2. **Low catalyst, high substrate** - long time course reveals slow deactivation pathways
3. **Very high substrate** - distinguishes M7 (second substrate binding) and M11/M16 (substrate-induced deactivation) from M1

The most discriminating single experiment: **high catalyst concentration (0.1 M)** with moderate substrate. This:
- Tests dimerization strongly (M2, M3, M13, M19) - these predict activity scaling less than linearly with [cat]
- Tests catalyst-based deactivation (M13 via 2cat, M19 via cat+catS)
- Distinguishes M6, M8 (cat activation) which depend differently on [cat]
- Will show whether rate scales linearly with catalyst
</hypothesis>
